quick: Sulfadoxine 1500 mg + pyrimethamine 75 mg as a single dose on day 1
summary: Sulfadoxine is a long-acting sulfonamide always given with pyrimethamine (SP). In India SP is the partner drug of artesunate (AS+SP) for uncomplicated falciparum malaria outside the North-East states, per the national drug policy, and SP is used for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy in some settings.
indications: Uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with artesunate (AS+SP), where SP is still effective
Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (programme use)

dosage.d: Sulfadoxine 1500 mg + pyrimethamine 75 mg as a single dose on day 1
dosage.n: With artesunate 4 mg/kg once daily for 3 days and primaquine per national policy

dosage.d: Sulfadoxine 25 mg/kg + pyrimethamine 1.25 mg/kg single dose (national age/weight bands)

admin: Use only as the finished product directs
moa: Sulfadoxine inhibits parasite dihydropteroate synthase; pyrimethamine inhibits dihydrofolate reductase. Sequential folate-pathway blockade.

relative: High-dose folic acid (5 mg) reduces efficacy

preg: Not in the first trimester; used in the second and third trimesters as IPTp where policy allows; low-dose folic acid (0.4 mg) may continue
lact: Avoid in breastfeeding infants under 2 months, jaundiced, ill or G6PD deficient infants

major: Co-trimoxazole and other antifolates: additive toxicity (do not combine)

serious: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis (can be fatal)
emergency: Any rash or mucosal lesions: stop and seek care

monitoring: Skin and mucosa for early SJS signs
counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: Supportive care; folinic acid for antifolate marrow toxicity; treat seizures.

footer: StewardMD-authored DRAFT. No US, Canadian or EU regulatory label exists for this molecule; AI-drafted from the references above and awaiting clinician review. Doses are typical published ranges, not a product label: check the Indian product's own pack insert before prescribing.
